item.content:encoded:
I know that this entry is old as dirt, but I still think this is worth saying.

IQ tests are a horrible method to use for actual scientific research, riddled with cultural bias. While they can still have some value in certain settings and for certain purposes, using them as an all-purpose general intelligence measure is incorrect. Not to say that the IQ test portion here should be removed, I'd just love to see an update on the wording so it's clear that The Foundation doesn't think IQ = how smart you are but they're using it as just one measure of many and it's being noted here because of the specific anomalous effect that manifested during it (or perhaps even just a footnote that says that there's a lot of internal debate amongst Foundation staff about the efficacy of such measurements, but it's being used here because the SCP in question has otherwise-human psychology and fits into the right cultural grouping to create a meaningful point of comparison, and/or because The Foundation lacks any better tools or measurements at this time that would be applicable to her).

EDIT: Oh also bump it up to Euclid to keep it in line with current guidelines regarding intelligent SCPs.

Changes that must happen in a good re-write of this article:

  • first off GET RID OF THE FOUNDATION PLANNING TO KILL HER. It is not harmful, the current foundation just loves to hoard SCPs. The current foundation killing it, a useful, harmless SCP, because they don't feel like paying it medical bill is completely idiotic.
  • If you noticed above, I was using the word "It", objectifying it. Thats what the foundation does in their papers about humanoid SCPs. They consider them objects. Get rid of the "her"s add "it"s, and do other things to make it sound more like an object. As Matilde Beiton said, it is to personal.
  • Letting her see SCPs in need of neutralization is not a problem because it 'will cause a reality threading paradox'. Reality held together just fine when she cheated on her tests. The foundation isn't stupid, they would see that it is worth the very minimal risk. On the other hand the chance of something in need of neutralization breaking out of containment and killing her or harming her because it is an Memetic/Cognitohazard/Infohazard, not to the paper work of arranging the tests, especially if it requires her to be moved to a different site. Also seeing SCPs that should be neutralized might be traumatizing. For example if foundation causes her to see SCP-231-7 in hopes of finding a way to end SCP-231-7's suffering SCP-187 might see Procedure 110-Montauk. Hopefully such a traumatizing incident as that can be cured with amnesiacs, but don't forget SCP-187's mind isn't exactly stable. Out of story it might cause the problem of neutralizing certain SCPs. Don't forget she is an irreplaceable and useful foundation asset.

Changes that might be good:

  • She is potentially an extremely useful SCP for aid in neutralizing SCPs the foundation wants to neutralize. As such it might be worthwhile to upgrade her to Thaumiel class. Remember, even the existence of the Thaumiel class is a secret from even most foundation personal. As such, the class change would require the rewrite to be extensive.
  • As I said above I think it would be better to make her wear a helmet that she can't take off because that would require a key. The helmet would have googles/visor that goes over her eyes, preventing them from being damage, a second visor, which can not be seen through, can be lowered over the transparent visor/googles. That way she could use her hands in an emergency. It would also help prevent her eyes from being damaged from unexpected external threats.

If anyone else has suggested changes that they think would be mandatory or simply good in a good rewrite please fill free to reply to this with your suggestions

item.content:encoded:
I liked this article when I joined, it being somewhere among the first 300 I read, and I still like it.

Let's face it , the tone is poor and there are a few downright dumb things, however, this was ported from old wiki - it's been here all the way since 2008, and I consider it rather unfair to judge old articles by new standards. The writing here isn't awful - It does a decent job exploring at least some of the aspects of precognition of this type that come to the reader's mind, and addressing in-universe issues in fairly sensible and inventive manner (eg. tied over eyes so that she doesn't gag on food) - something that's a defining characteristic of the Foundation. And as for the idea, it's downright great. This is one of the iconic "oh Bast does it suck to be them" humanoid articles used as an example of one of the ways an effective humanoid SCP can be written up in at least one guide.

Rewriting this one would be a lot like grabbing Jules Verne's novels and editting them for scientific accuracy, that said, with a score (+68 as I seen it last) that's above average even these days, it luckily isn't at risk of such treatment.

Rather than taking tests with pencil and paper, since she's a risk to her own safety, perhaps a paper printout connected to a mittens-friendly testing computer could be arranged. One at a time the questions would be printed dot-matrix style and then feed out a bit. She would see the future state of the paper printed, type her answer, and the printer would retract into the printer and then print her answer, thereby completing the future state, and then move onto the next question.

Also, can she "ace" an intelligence test if it is printed in a language that she doesn't understand by seeing its future state alone, or must she know the language in question? If knowledge of the language is irrelevant she could, in theory anyway, be asked questions that she can't possibly know the answer for. Perhaps asking in Greek how SPC-682 can be permanently contained or something? Or maybe asking in hieroglyphics some variation of "where is the information contained in your answers coming from?"
